title: Umbrella Check
summary: A single static page that answers one question: do I need an umbrella tomorrow? It asks the browser for the visitor's location (or takes a city name), fetches tomorrow's forecast from Open-Meteo without any key, and shows a big yes or no with the chance of rain, the expected rainfall and the rule it used.
architecture: index.html loads app.js (page logic). app.js imports forecast.mjs, a pure module that builds the request URLs, reads tomorrow's values and decides the verdict. styles.css holds the layout. README.md explains how to use it.
assumptions: Location: Ask the browser for the location; if that is refused, let the visitor type a city
When to take an umbrella: Yes when tomorrow's chance of rain is 40% or more, or at least 1 mm of rain is expected

acceptance.description: index.html has the title and a city input
The page has a search form and a result area
The forecast request asks for tomorrow's daily rain values with timezone=auto
60% chance of rain gives 'Take an umbrella'; 10% and 0 mm gives 'No umbrella needed'
The verdict is clear to a non-technical reader and shows the rule used
acceptance.rubric: Plain words; shows chance of rain, expected rainfall and the 40% / 1 mm rule
